questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

It is not uncommon

P. for parents and others in a particular animal

Q. group to teach their young through example how to

R. of drought or other environmental change

S. find food or water when it becomes scarce because
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **sentence discusses the behavior observed** in a particular animal group where parents and others teach their young how to find food or water when it becomes scarce due to drought or other environmental changes.
 
• This order of the sentence provides a logical flow of information,** starting with the subject (P) **introducing the parents and others, **followed by** the purpose of teaching through example **(Q)**.
 
• **Then,** it describes the **specific situation (S)** where food or water becomes scarce, and **finally,** it mentions t**he cause or reason (R)** for the scarcity, which is drought or other environmental change.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: **'PQSR'.**

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Tina said, "My parents are getting divorced."

options.text: Tina said that her parents are getting divorced.
Tina said that her parents were get divorced.
Tina said that her parents have been getting divorce.
Tina said that her parents were getting divorced.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When** reporting someone's statement** in indirect speech, we **usually change **the verb tense to reflect the shift in time.
 
• **In this case, **the original statement is in the present tense ("My parents are getting divorced"), so when we report it indirectly, we need to change the verb tense to past tense.
 
• **'Option 4'** correctly changes the verb tense to past tense, reflecting the shift from the original statement.
 
• The **past progressive tense** ("were getting divorced") **indicates **an ongoing action in the past.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: * "Tina said that her parents were getting divorced".*

questions.question:

French is been spoken here by Suresh.

• **To convert this** sentence into the passive form,** we need to** make the object "French" the subject and the subject "Suresh" the object of the sentence.
 
• In the passive voice,** the structure is**: Object + is/are + past participle + by + subject.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'French is spoken here by Suresh.'*

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To lay someone by the heels
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option(1) i.e. To confine somebody in prison**.

• **Example:** The notorious criminal was finally laid by the heels after a long pursuit.
 
 
 
• **"To confine somebody in prison"** refers to putting someone in jail or under restraint. (किसी को जेल में बंद करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The thief was laid by the heels after being caught red-handed.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the meaning of the idiom **'To lay someone by the heels'** is best expressed by **Option(1)**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option(1) i.e. To confine somebody in prison**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
